title: Best API Integration Developers (2026): How to Hire One
description: How to hire a developer to connect your apps and tools through APIs: what to include, how to brief it, price factors and red flags.
intro: Integration developers connect the tools you already use, such as your store, CRM, email platform or accounting software, so data flows between them without copy and paste. Good integrations save hours every week. They go wrong when nobody plans for errors, keys are stored carelessly, or the integration depends on the developer's own accounts. This guide helps you set up connections that keep working.

faq.a: An API is a way for one piece of software to talk to another, for example to send a new order from your store to your accounting tool. Most modern tools offer one.

faq.q: Should I use a no-code tool instead?
faq.a: Tools like Zapier or Make work well for simple connections. Custom code makes sense for high volumes, complex rules or tools the no-code services do not support. Ask the developer which fits your case.

faq.q: What happens when an integration fails?
faq.a: Ask how errors are detected and reported, and what happens to data that fails to sync. A good integration logs errors and alerts someone.
You should. Create keys in your own accounts, share them securely, and rotate them if a developer leaves.
Ask for a short description of what connects to what, how often it runs, where it is hosted and how to restart it.
